requirements: Auto Persona resolution must prioritize actor-type defaults over stack hints and always resolve `auto` to an effective persona with reason.
Simple help must simplify explanation without renaming or mutating canonical model semantics.
Expert and ELI5 help variants must share the same concept skeleton and differ only in phrasing density.
Project cards must distinguish health vs activity vs attention, and treat historical-only activity as non-degraded unless explicitly archived.
Resurfacing should be change/persistence-based (severity/owner/duration/actionability), not heartbeat spam.
Dense Orchestrator tabs must use slice loading, virtualization, lazy expansion, and demand-loading; exact ledger inspection still paged.
Bulk actions should default to navigation/triage/low-risk updates; high-risk runtime mutations require explicit safe batch semantics.
Mutation controls must be gated by trusted projection state (`current`) or canonical runtime revalidation.
decisions: Split help model into canonical term system, help entry system, and contextual help system.
Use glossary as canonical short-definition backbone; richer help entries carry examples and related links.
Use a project-summary projection with compact singular status emphasizing dominant owner and primary reason.
Adopt shared escalation ladder: info -> warning -> attention_required -> blocked -> system_notification.
Treat scale and projection-trust behavior as Orchestrator-wide contracts, not per-tab ad hoc rules.
Keep command palette universal for navigation but guarded for mutation-bearing runtime actions.
data_shapes: Help entry template: canonical name, short definition, why it matters, what it is not, related states/actions, related concepts, where seen.
Project card model: Activity (`idle|running|paused|queued|background_active`), Attention (`none|attention_required|blocked|degraded`), plus Health.
Shared routing payload: `project_id`, `focused_run_id`, destination tab, selected object id/type, optional inspector target, optional filters.
routing_rules: Concept-help links should connect related clusters (e.g., seam/work-package/integration, promotion/revocation/reopen, lane/worktree lifecycle).
Projects page should deep-link pressure/attention summaries into Usage, Authentication, Orchestrator, and detail tabs.
Escalation surface mapping: History gets full chronology; Progress/Dashboard active severity; badges compressed counts; chat for user decisions; sparse system notifications.
Fallback ladder under stale/degraded trust: widget summary -> native tab; rollup -> filtered record slice; inspector -> Ledger/History/detail-ref view.
Context menus should expose only object-valid canonical actions; palette/shortcuts must honor same confirmation gates.
verification_rules: `auto` cannot remain opaque; historical runs must preserve resolved effective persona/reason at execution time.
`attention_required` and `blocked` must remain distinct; persistent blockers cannot be dismissed into fake health.
Confirmation strength cannot be downgraded by action discoverability (palette/shortcut/context).
Stale visibility is not action authority; stale `allowed_action_ids[]` must not be trusted without revalidation.
owner_consumer_obligations: When attention/blocked is shown, surface dominant current owner (Runtime, Package Overseer, Seam Overseer, Corroboration, Graph Patch, Recovery, User, External Resource).
Project summaries should communicate one primary reason and optional additional-issues count, avoiding mini-dashboard overload.
System notifications should be reserved for sparse high-value events (HITL required, completion, major failure, severe execution-blocking pressure).
stale_retirement_items: Retire setup-centric single-dot status semantics that conflate health with attention.
Retire tooltip-only concept-help assumptions for rewrite-era first-class terms.
Retire graph-only scaling assumptions; enforce equivalent density controls on Seams/Evidence/History/Ledger.
Retire broad implicit bulk-mutation affordances without explicit action-surface classification.
open_questions: What explicit policy determines which concepts get full help entries versus contextual-only help?
What exact thresholds drive resurfacing cadence by severity and persistence?
What Orchestrator-wide defaults define initial slice sizes, paging/search interplay, and cross-tab inspector loading?
What concrete action matrix classifies palette-visible, shortcut-eligible, context-menu-only, and bulk-forbidden commands?
process_defects: Concept-help contract is underdefined; risk of inconsistent term redefinition across surfaces.
Projects status model remains too setup-centric and lacks a canonical blocked-owner/primary-reason rollup.
Escalation behavior exists as fragmented case rules, not a single cross-surface contract.
Scale and trust policies are uneven across tabs; mutation gating under stale/degraded projections is not uniformly specified.
